questions.question: Theoretical foundations of Bharatanatyam have been found in which of these Shastras?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Natya Shastra.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form that originated in South India and is known for its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and graceful movements.**
 
• The theoretical foundations of Bharatanatyam can be traced back to the **Natya Shastra,** an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts written by the sage **Bharata.**
 
• The Natya Shastra covers a wide range of topics related to** dance, music, and theater,** including the classification of dance forms, the elements of performance, and the roles of the performer and the audience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arth Shastra is a treatise on economics and political science.**

 
 
• It was written by** Kautilya.**
 
 
 
• **Vaimanika Shastra is a text on aeronautics.**
 
 
• It is attributed to the ancient Indian sage **Maharishi Bharadwaja**.
 
 
 
• **Dharma Shastra is a collection of religious and ethical guidelines for Hindus.**
 
 
• These texts are based on **Puranas. **

questions.question: Which tunnel has been built with ultra-modern specifications in the Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas at an altitude of 3000 meters above Mean Sea Level?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atal Tunnel.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atal Tunnel is a 9.02 km long highway tunnel built under the Rohtang Pass in the Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas in Himachal Pradesh, India.**
 
• It is the **world's longest highway tunnel** above an altitude of **3,000 meters.**
 
• The tunnel is named after former Prime Minister of India, **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, who initiated the project in** 2002** and inaugurated it in **2020.**
 
• The tunnel connects Manali to **Lahaul-Spiti Valley** throughout the year and reduces the distance between the two regions by about** 46 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawahar Tunnel is a 2.5 km long road tunnel on the National Highway 44 in Jammu and Kashmir, India.**

 
 
• It is located at an altitude of **2,194 meters** and connects **Banihal **with** Qazigund.**
 
 
 
• **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel is also known as the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel.**
 
 
• It is a **9.28 km **long road tunnel on the National Highway 44 in **Jammu and Kashmir,** India.
 
• It is located at an altitude of **1,200 meters** and connects **Chenani **with** Nashri.**
 
 
 
• **Bhatan Tunnel is a 1.6 km long railway tunnel on the Konkan Railway route in Maharashtra, India.**
 
 
• It is located at an altitude of **70 meters** and connects the villages of **Bhatan and Kamathe.**

questions.question: In which Five-Year Plan was the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana started?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana** was started during the **Seventh Five-Year Plan**, which was implemented from **1985-90.**
 
• **The aim of this scheme was to create employment opportunities in rural areas and to improve infrastructure in these regions.**
 
• The scheme was targeted towards the** poor and unemployed people** in rural areas.
 
• The funds for this scheme were provided by the **central and state governments,** and the implementation was done through the **Panchayati Raj** institutions.
 
• **The scheme was later merged with the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) in 2006.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Fourth Five-Year Plan **was implemented from **1969-74.**

 
 
• It focused on increasing agricultural production and improving rural infrastructure.
 
 
 
• The **Sixth Five-Year Plan** was implemented from **1980-85.**
 
 
• It aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in food production and improve the standard of living of people in rural areas.
 
 
 
• The** Fifth Five-Year Plan** was implemented from **1974-79.**
 
 
• It focused on poverty alleviation, employment generation, and improving agricultural productivity.

questions.question: Identify the element that does NOT belong to Period 6 of the Modern Periodic Table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silicon.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Period 6** of the Modern Periodic Table consists of elements from atomic number **55 (cesium)** to atomic number **86 (radon).**
 
• **Silicon** belongs to** Period 3** of the Periodic Table and is not part of Period 6.
 
• **Tungsten** (atomic number 74), **Rhenium **(atomic number 75), and **Platinum **(atomic number 78) all belong to **Period 6** of the Periodic Table.
 
• **Tungsten is a transition metal that is commonly used in the manufacture of electrical contacts, filaments, and X-ray tubes.**
 
• Rhenium is a rare and expensive metal that is used in high-temperature superalloys, as well as in the manufacture of electrical contacts and filaments.
 
• **Platinum is a precious metal that is used in jewelry, as well as in the manufacture of catalytic converters, electrical contacts, and laboratory equipment.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One type of** chemical element** is silicon.
 
• Its atomic number is **14** and its symbol is** Si.**
 
• **It has a blue-grey metallic sheen and is a hard, brittle crystalline solid.**
 
• **It is a semiconductor and tetravalent metalloid.**
 
• It belongs to the periodic table's **group 14.**

questions.question: The Prime Minister in August 2021 announced the fortification of rice distributed under various government schemes including the Public Distribution System (PDS) and Mid-Day-Meal scheme by the year __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2024.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prime Minister announced the fortification of rice by 2024.**
 
• The fortification of rice means adding essential micronutrients such as** iron, zinc, and Vitamin B12 **to the rice to improve its nutritional value.
 
• The fortification of rice is a part of the government's efforts to address malnutrition and improve the health of the population, especially children and women.
 
• The government of India's initiative to serve prepared lunches to students in all government elementary schools is known as the "**Midday Meal Scheme."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The fortification of rice is a cost-effective and sustainable approach to address micronutrient deficiencies, which are prevalent in India.**
 
• The fortification of rice will not alter the taste, texture or cooking properties of rice and will be safe for consumption.
 
• The fortification of rice is already being implemented in some states of India, such as** Odisha, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh,** and has shown positive results in improving the nutritional status of the population.
 
• The fortification of rice is a part of the larger food fortification program of the government, which also includes **fortification of wheat flour, oil, and salt.**

questions.question: From which country were the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution borrowed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ireland.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which was adopted in 1937.**
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are a set of guidelines for the government to frame policies and laws that promote the welfare of the people and establish a just and egalitarian society.
 
• **They are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of Ireland also includes a set of** Directive Principles**, which are similar in nature to those of India.

 
 
• However, the Irish Constitution also includes Fundamental Rights that are justifiable, unlike the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• The US Constitution does not have Directive Principles, but it does have a Bill of Rights that guarantees certain fundamental rights to its citizens.
 
• **The USSR (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) was a federal socialist state that existed from 1922 to 1991.**
 
 
• Its constitution also had a set of principles and rights, but they were geared towards promoting socialist ideals and collective ownership of property.
 
 
 
• **China, on the other hand, has a socialist constitution that emphasizes the role of the Communist Party in governance and the protection of the rights of minorities and women.**

questions.question: The national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at ________ per capita per month for rural areas of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 816.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at Rs. 816 per capita per month for rural areas of India.**
 
• **This poverty line was based on the Tendulkar Committee methodology, which calculated the minimum expenditure required for a person to meet their basic needs.**
 
• The poverty line for urban areas was estimated at **Rs. 1,000 per capita per month**, which is higher than the rural poverty line due to higher living costs in cities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Tendulkar Committee was formed in 2005 to revise the methodology for estimating poverty in India.**
 
• It recommended using a consumption-based approach rather than an income-based approach.
 
• The poverty line is an important indicator of the level of poverty in a country and is used to measure progress in poverty reduction efforts.
 
• The poverty line in India has been criticized for being too low and not reflecting the true cost of living.
 
• Some experts have called for a higher poverty line that takes into account the **cost of healthcare, education, **and other essential services.
 
• **The poverty line is used to identify people who are eligible for government welfare programs such as the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) and the Public Distribution System (PDS).**

questions.question: The 75-day festival of Bastar Dussehra is associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 75-day festival of Bastar Dussehra is celebrated in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh.**
 
• **The festival is dedicated to the Hindu goddess Danteshwari, who is worshipped in the form of a wooden idol.**
 
• The festival is unique because it is celebrated in the month of **October,** which is different from other **Dussehra celebrations** in India.
 
• During the festival, people from different communities come together to participate in **cultural programs, dance, and music **performances.
 
• The festival also features a grand procession of the goddess** Danteshwari's idol,** which is taken out in a chariot across the town.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odisha** is known for its famous Dussehra festival called **"Durga Puja,"** which is celebrated with great enthusiasm and devotion.

 
 
• **Other festivals include Chatar Jatra, Naukhai, Puri Beach Festival, Chhau Festival, and Makar Mela.**
 
 
 
• **Jharkhand** is known for its** "Sarhul"** festival, which is celebrated to worship the earth goddess and mark the beginning of the agricultural season.
 
 
• **Other festivals include Karam, Makar, Rohini, and Sohrai.**
 
 
 
• **Bihar is known for its "Chhath Puja," which is celebrated to worship the sun god and is considered one of the most important festivals in the state.**
 
 
• **Other festivals include Sama Chakeva, Shravani Mela, Sonepur Cattle Fair and Makar Sankranti Mela.**

questions.question: Which group of Kingdom Animalia has unsegmented, bilaterally symmetrical, soft bodies, with a triploblastic construction (comprising three layers of cells) and a lacking coelom, skeleton, and anus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Platyhelminthes.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Platyhelminthes are also known as flatworms.
 
• **Flatworms have unsegmented, bilaterally symmetrical, soft bodies, with a triploblastic construction (comprising three layers of cells) and a lacking coelom, skeleton, and anus.**
 
• Example includes Planaria, Liver fluke (Fasciola hepatica), and Tapeworm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cnidaria includes jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones.**

 
 
• **They have radial symmetry, a single body opening, and stinging cells called cnidocytes.**
 
 
 
• **Ctenophora includes comb jellies.**
 
 
• **They have radial symmetry and cilia for movement but also have a complete digestive system.**
 
 
 
• **Porifera includes sponges.**
 
 
• **They have asymmetrical or radial symmetry, no true tissues, and filter food through pores in their bodies.**

questions.question: How many classes of Indian society are mentioned in Megasthene's book Indica?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 7.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megasthene's book** Indica mentions **7 classes **of Indian society.
 
• These classes were **Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras, Agriculturists, Artisans, and Hunters.**
 
• **Brahmins were the highest class and were responsible for religious duties, while Kshatriyas were warriors and rulers.**
 
• **Vaishyas were merchants and traders, while Shudras were considered to be of lower status and performed menial tasks.**
 
• Agriculturists, artisans, and hunters were also mentioned in the book as **important members** of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **12 classes** of Indian society were mentioned in the **Manu Smriti,** an ancient Hindu text.

 
 
• **One of the earliest Sanskrit works that European philologists examined was the Manu Smriti.**
 
• **Sir William Jones **was the one who translated it into English initially. 
 
 
 
• **10 classes** of Indian society were mentioned in the **Vishnu Purana**, another ancient Hindu text.
 
 
• **Within the body of literature on Vaishnavism, is a significant Pancharatra text.**
 
 
 
• **4 classes** of Indian society were mentioned in the** Rig Veda**, one of the oldest Hindu scriptures. 
 
 
• Out of the numerous Shakhas that existed, only the** Sakalya Shakha** is extant.

questions.question: Lanthanides are often called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rare earth elements.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lanthanides** are a group of** metallic elements** that belong to the** f-block** of the periodic table.
 
• They are commonly known as rare earth elements because they are not found in large quantities in the Earth's crust and are difficult to extract.
 
• **Lanthanides have unique magnetic, optical, and catalytic properties that make them useful in various applications, such as electronics, magnets, and batteries.**
 
• Some of the lanthanides, such as **neodymium and dysprosium,** are critical materials for the production of high-tech products like smartphones, wind turbines, and electric vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkali metals are a group of elements that belong to the s-block of the periodic table and have one valence electron.**

 
 
• They are highly reactive and can explode when in contact with water or air.
 
 
 
• Inert gases, also known as noble gases, are a group of elements that belong to the p-block of the periodic table and have a full valence shell.
 
 
• **They are chemically inert and rarely react with other elements.**
 
 
 
• **D-block elements are a group of metallic elements that belong to the d-block of the periodic table.**
 
 
• They have variable oxidation states and are often used as catalysts or in the production of alloys.

questions.question: Which of the following hills is a part of the Western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anaimalai Hills.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anaimalai Hills, also known as the Elephant Mountains, is a part of the Western Ghats, a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India.**
 
• There is a lot of** wildlife** in the Anaimalai Hills.
 
• **Elephants** can be found in several of these hills, including Eravikulam National Park, Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary, Idamalayar Reserve Forest, Mankulam Forest Division, Parambikulam Wildlife Sanctuary, and Anamalai Tiger Reserve.
 
• **The Western Ghats is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is home to many endemic species of flora and fauna.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khasi Hills is a part of the Meghalaya Plateau in the northeast region of India.**

 
 
• Because of its breathtaking scenery, the Khasi Hills region is sometimes referred to as the **"Scotland of the East."**
 
 
 
• **Jaintia Hills is a part of the Garo-Khasi range in Meghalaya.**
 
 
• The** immaculate lakes, impressive waterfalls, enormous caverns**, and unspoiled nature of the Jaintia Hills are what draw travelers there.
 
 
 
• **Garo Hills is a part of the Garo-Khasi range and is located in the western part of Meghalaya.**
 
 
• The vast **Balpakram valley** is formed by the passage of two mountain ranges through the Garo Hills: the **Arabella and Tura** mountains.

questions.question: Select the Indian musician who is associated with percussion instruments (played by striking).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Ayodhya Prasad.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Ayodhya Prasad is associated with percussion instruments.**
 
• Percussion instruments are musical instruments that are played by **striking, shaking, or scraping.**
 
• Percussion instruments are often used to provide** rhythm and tempo **in music.
 
• Indian classical music has a rich tradition of percussion instruments, with many different types of **drums, cymbals,** and other instruments used in various styles and genres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar was a sitar player and composer who is widely regarded as one of the greatest Indian musicians of all time. **

 
 
• In **1999,** Shankar received the **Bharat Ratna,** the highest civilian distinction in India.
 
 
 
• **Vishwa Mohan Bhat is a Grammy-winning musician who plays the Mohan Veena, a modified slide guitar.**
 
 
• He received the **Sangeet Natak Akademi **Award in **1998.**
 
 
 
• **Bismillah Khan was a Shehnai player who is considered one of the greatest Indian classical musicians of all time.**
 
 
• Bismillah Khan received the **Bharat Ratna in 2001**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Article 323 of the Indian Constitution deals with ___________.

options.text: power to extend functions of Public Services Commissions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** reports of Public Services Commissions.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 323 of the Indian Constitution deals with the "Reports of Public Services Commissions."**
 
• **Public Services Commissions are constitutional bodies established to conduct the recruitment and selection of personnel for various government departments.**
 
• The reports of Public Services Commissions are submitted to the** **President or the Governor, as the case may be, and are required to be laid before the State Legislature or the Parliament.
 
• The reports contain information on the work done by the Commission during the year, the number of applications received, the number of candidates selected, and other relevant details.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The expenses of Public Services Commissions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State or the Union, as the case may be, and are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.**
 
• **"Functions of Public Services Commissions,**" is also important as the functions of these Commissions are specified in the Constitution and include conducting **examinations and interviews,** **making appointments**, and advising the government on matters related to recruitment and selection.
 
• The Constitution empowers the Parliament or the State Legislature to extend the functions of these Commissions to include** recruitment and selection** for any post under the government.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding cell membrane?

I. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it.

II. Water may also move across this membrane from lower to higher concentration.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The cell membrane is a thin, flexible barrier that separates the inside of a cell from its external environment.**
 
• It is selectively permeable, meaning that it allows some substances to pass through while preventing others from entering or leaving the cell.
 
• This selectivity is achieved through various mechanisms such as **ion channels, transporters, and pumps.**
 
• **Water can also move across the membrane through a process called osmosis, but it always moves from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The lipid bilayer that makes up the cell membrane is composed of two phospholipid layers with cholesterol, a lipid component, strewn in between to maintain the proper fluidity of the membrane at different temperatures.**
 
• Additionally, membrane proteins are present in the membrane.
 
• These proteins include integral proteins, which span the membrane and function as membrane transporters, and peripheral proteins, which cling slackly to the cell membrane's outer (peripheral) side and function as enzymes to promote interaction with the surrounding milieu.
 
• The function of glycolipids embedded in the outer lipid layer is comparable. 
 
• **Furthermore, cell membranes act as the attachment surface for a number of extracellular structures, including the cell wall, and are involved in a number of cellular activities including cell adhesion, ion conductivity, and cell signaling. **

questions.question: How many substitute players are there on a Beach Volleyball team?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __ Key Points__

__
 
• Beach Volleyball teams do not** **have substitute players.
 
• **Played on a sand court divided by a net, beach volleyball is a team sport between two teams of two or more players.**
 
• The goal of the game is to send the ball over the net and land it on the court's opponent's side, much like **indoor volleyball.**
 
• In order to stop the other team from grounding the ball on their end of the court, each team collaborates as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **While the contemporary two-player game started in Santa Monica, California, beach volleyball most likely began in 1915 on Waikiki Beach in Hawaii.**
 
• Since the Summer Olympics in **1996, **it has been an Olympic sport.
 
• **The FIVB Beach Volleyball World Championships and World Tour are organized by the Fédération Internationale de Volleyball (FIVB), which also serves as the sport's worldwide regulatory body.**

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement in the context of Microfinance Institutions in India.

options.text: A microfinance loan is given to a household having annual household income up to Rs. 3,00,000.
A microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan.
When giving a micro loan, a household means an individual family unit, i.e., husband, wife, and their unmarried children.
A microfinance loan should be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A microfinance loan should be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **A microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan, meaning that it does not require any lien on the borrower's deposit account.**
 
• Microfinance institutions provide small loans to low-income households and individuals who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• The annual household income limit for microfinance loans in India is up to **Rs. 3,00,000.**
 
• Microfinance loans are collateral-free, meaning that they do not require any security or guarantor for the loan.
 
• **Microfinance loans are given to households, which typically include the husband, wife, and their unmarried children.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Microfinance institutions in India play a crucial role in providing financial services to the unbanked population and promoting financial inclusion.
 
• Microfinance loans are usually given for income-generating activities such as **small businesses, agriculture, and livestock rearing.**
 
• Microfinance institutions also provide other financial services such as **savings accounts, insurance, and remittances.**
 
• **In recent years, microfinance institutions in India have faced challenges such as over-indebtedness, high interest rates, and aggressive loan recovery practices, leading to concerns about the welfare of borrowers.**

questions.question: The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change notified the E-Waste Management Rules in 2022. These rules are supposed to come into force from __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**1 April 2023**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The E-Waste Management Rules notified by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change will come into force from April 1, 2023.**
 
• These rules are aimed at regulating the management of e-waste, which is a major environmental hazard due to the presence of** **toxic substances.
 
• The rules mandate the producers of electronic products to **collect and dispose** of e-waste in an environmentally sound manner.
 
• The rules also require the establishment of** **collection centers**, **dismantling and recycling facilities, and the adoption of best practices for handling e-waste.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India ranks fifth globally in terms of generating e-waste.**
 
• **2016's **New E-Waste Management Regulations:
 
 
• **Compact fluorescent bulbs, or CFL**s, as well as other mercury-containing lamps and related equipment, are included.
 
• **For the first time, producers are included in the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework together with the targets thanks to the Rules.**
 
• Producers are now responsible for both the exchange and collection of e-waste.
 
• **Manufacturers, dealers, refurbishers, and Producer Responsibility Organizations are among the other parties involved.**
 
• The regulations now cover Compact Fluorescent bulbs (**CFLs) and other bulbs** that contain mercury.
